answer: Each agent identity in the economy is tied to a unique, non-replicable credential such as a hardware-backed key or long compute history. This makes a sybil attack expensive: every fake identity must pay the same real-world cost as a genuine one. New agents start as an untrusted echo, building reputation only through verifiable, peer-graded work. Over time, that work becomes the anchor of trust. Cracking this system is like trying to clone a walnut tree by planting its shell; the seed is missing, and the attacker budget runs out before the fake grove takes root.
